designs.understanding: Funding has three pure functions (score_readiness, match_investors, analyze_gaps) and a pipeline metric function, but none distinguishes 'the founder did not tell us' from 'the founder said no'. Funding.tsx fills the gap by hard-coding fourteen answers (has_ip, retention 60, runway 12, unit economics, cap table, ...) 'so a complete founder profile scores realistically'; readiness counts them, and match_investors uses the resulting overall as a hard gate (readiness_gate: 60, or 70 for late stages) that no investor published. The investor side has the same flaw in reverse: an investor with no published stages or sectors is rejected ('not published' treated as 'no'), and _fit is 60% constants (stage always 100, geography always 100 because real_investors() sets every geography to Tamil Nadu, track record a neutral default). analyze_gaps only receives the ReadinessResult, not the profile, so it cannot know what is already done, and its impact_points are hand-typed numbers that disagree with the rubric weights. In pipeline.py a terminal entry with no history is inferred to have passed every open stage, and date.fromisoformat cannot parse the ISO datetime the board stamps, so first-stage time is dropped. Root cause: no notion of an unknown input and no single rubric definition from which scoring, coverage, gating and gap advice all derive. All five flags hold; line numbers cited for investor_match.py are stale (file is 127 lines) but the logic is unchanged.

flags_disputed.note: Evidence cites investor_match.py:220/279; the file is now 127 lines and the gate sits in readiness_gate()/_violations(). Logic and the 0-eligible outcome still hold.

The fix relies on Python 3.11 datetime.fromisoformat accepting 'Z', but pyproject declares requires-python >=3.10 / target py310, where 'Z' is rejected. Normalise 'Z' to '+00:00' explicitly. Also, 'terminal entries without history count only their terminal stage' is too strict for closed_won: can_advance allows WON only from term_sheet/negotiation and open stages advance one at a time, so WON provably implies every open stage through term_sheet. Only LOST should count as its terminal stage alone.

approaches.name: Single rubric table with three-valued inputs
approaches.how: Replace the six hand-written scorers with one RUBRIC table of (dimension, input, kind flag|number|stage, points or scale+cap). A typed FundingProfile has every input Optional (None = not told). Scoring walks the table: each dimension returns points plus coverage = answered weight / total weight; under 50% coverage a dimension is 'not assessed'. The same table drives gap counterfactuals and the 'what to answer next' list.
approaches.basis: Data-driven rubric mirrors the scheme engine's rules over facts; three-valued unknown is the pattern T04 adopts for schemes.
approaches.advantages: One definition feeds score, coverage, gaps and questions so they cannot disagree; honest about missing answers; pure and property-testable.
approaches.drawbacks: Scores drop for founders who skip questions (intended); one-time rewrite of readiness.py and its tests.

approaches.drawbacks: A 25-field form on a 2G phone for low-literacy founders; answers typed to get past the form are invented data by another route.

approaches.basis: The conversation already collects stage, team and experience (elicitation PROFILE_SLOTS).

approaches.drawbacks: Covers about 5 of 25 inputs; still needs an unknown state for the rest, so it is an input source, not a fix.

approaches.how: Encode investor constraints and fit as a CP-SAT model and rank by objective.
approaches.basis: OR-Tools is installed and used by the roadmap selector.
approaches.drawbacks: One startup against N independent investors has no combinatorial structure; adds latency and opacity to a per-row check the module docstring already says needs no solver.

approaches.basis: Small popular pure-Python library; thesis is the richest text field.
approaches.advantages: Uses real investor text instead of constants.
approaches.drawbacks: 36 one-paragraph summaries give noisy scores; a new dependency; similarity is hard to explain to a founder.

approaches.drawbacks: No outcome data for TN founders exists; any fitted number today would be invented.

designs.chosen: Single rubric table with three-valued inputs, plus slot projection as an optional, origin-tagged input source; investor constraints three-valued with readiness demoted to advice; counterfactual gaps from the same rubric; standard-library pipeline fixes.
designs.why_chosen: It fixes the shared root (no unknown, no single rubric) once and every symptom follows: the frontend needs no invented defaults because unknown is legal; gap impact is exact because it re-runs the same pure scorer; coverage tells the founder what to answer next; readiness can only rank and advise because hard constraints are reserved for what investors publish. Slot projection plugs in behind the same typed profile so 'never ask twice' improves without being load-bearing. Deterministic, offline, standard library only.

design.components: 1) funding/rubric.py: RUBRIC rows and FundingProfile (Pydantic, every field Optional, plus origin map field->'founder'|'conversation'). 2) readiness.py: score_readiness(profile) -> ReadinessResult{dimensions: {dim: {score|None, coverage, missing}}, overall|None, assessed_weight, band|'not enough answers', next_inputs (top 3 missing by weight)}. 3) investor_match.py: each criterion returns yes|no|unknown; result has eligible, check_with_investor (no 'no', at least one 'unknown', e.g. stage or sector not published), ineligible. readiness_gate deleted; readiness shown as advice beside the list. 4) _fit uses only varying terms: sector (specialist in founder's canonical sector 100, generalist 70), ticket position (when ticket known: need in middle half 100, edge 70), traction margin (only where min_users/min_revenue published), thesis overlap (T01 canonical keywords found in thesis, capped). Terms without data are omitted and weights renormalised; fit carries 'why' strings; ties broken by name. 5) gaps.py: each PLAYBOOK action names its input change ({'is_registered': True}, {'stage': 'mvp'}) and a precondition; analyze_gaps(profile, readiness) drops actions already satisfied, marks actions on unknown inputs 'if not done yet', impact = rubric re-score delta. Effort weeks stay curated but labelled estimates. 6) pipeline.py: _reached: history -> stages in history; no history: LOST -> {LOST}; WON -> open stages through term_sheet + WON; open -> stages up to current. _to_date helper ('Z'->'+00:00', datetime.fromisoformat(...).date(), else date.fromisoformat). STAGE_PROBABILITY and weighted_value removed. 7) Funding.tsx: tri-state toggles (yes / no / not sure, default not sure); sends only founder-set fields; shows coverage, 'not assessed' and the 'check with the investor' group.
design.data_model: FundingProfile: stage: Stage|None (T01 enum); team_size, founder_experience_years, advisors_count, users, monthly_revenue, retention_rate, partnerships, runway_months, revenue_growth_pct, feature_completeness, deck_completeness: number|None; has_*/is_*/dpiit_recognized: bool|None. RubricRow(dimension, input, kind, points|scale, cap). DimensionScore{score|None, coverage, missing}. InvestorMatchResult{eligible:[{investor, fit, why}], check_with_investor:[{investor, unknown}], ineligible:[{investor, reasons}], total_checked}. Recommendation{dimension, action, changes, impact_points, effort_weeks, conditional}. funding_schemas.py updated; readiness_overall becomes an optional advice input to matching.
design.algorithm: Unanswered rows add to the dimension's total weight but earn nothing; dimension score is earned points on the existing full scale (no inflation by renormalising within a dimension); coverage reported separately; coverage < 0.5 -> score None. overall = weighted mean over assessed dimensions with weights renormalised; assessed weight < 0.5 -> overall None, band 'not enough answers'. Gap impact(a) = score(profile with a.changes).overall - score(profile with a's inputs set falsy).overall, computed with every dimension forced assessed so impact reflects rubric points. Sort by impact/effort, ties by dimension weight.
design.interfaces: T01: Stage and Sector enums for profile.stage, investor stages/sectors and thesis keywords. T04: reuse its three-valued Verdict type rather than define a second. T30: the server profile (nullable founder/startup columns) is the future source of stage/team facts; self-reported origin is never called verified. T19: conversation-sourced fields only when the consent purpose covers reuse. Pipeline metrics are consumed by the 3.1.3 server board and 5.5.5 programme aggregates.
design.rollout: Backend first, accepting old full payloads and partial ones (missing = unknown); then Funding.tsx stops sending defaults; then remove weighted_value from Pipeline.tsx. Saved localStorage boards keep loading because date parsing becomes more tolerant.
design.offline: Deterministic Python over local ecosystem JSON; no model or network. Nothing degrades.

Rotation: scripts/rotate_keys.py re-encrypts rows whose kid is not active in idempotent batches; blind index key rotates only with a full recompute.

designs.understanding: Housekeeping (cache purge, warming, retention, erasure, cohort rebuild) is planned as an out-of-process scripts/nightly.py, but Settings resolve research_cache_dir and env_file against the working directory (two caches already exist, repo root and backend/), so a script started elsewhere purges the wrong cache and sees no DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL. Deleting a session through the inner store from another process leaves the CachedStore Redis copy (6 h TTL) and the app's in-memory job board. There is no user-to-data map: agent_sessions.user_id is a free string, 'anon' on every row, users.founder_id points the wrong way for cascades, and a delete-all for 'anon' would erase everyone. SYSTEM-DESIGN 5.4 both deletes consents on erasure and keeps them a year after the data. Nothing records runs, prevents overlap or counts failures. Root cause: no in-app maintenance service owns 'delete this person or this expired data everywhere' and 'run nightly work once and record it'. All six flags hold.

flags_disputed.note: The leak comes from deleting through the inner store: CachedStore.delete already drops sess:{id}. A process using get_store() (full stack) clears Redis; only the in-memory job board needs the app process. This supports running maintenance in the app, and makes a standalone fallback safe when the app is down (no memory to clear).
Agree with OS-scheduler-only triggering, but it is not zero code: catch-up after a sleeping laptop and manual overlapping runs still need F-B5-013's lock and ledger, so the two flags are one design.

design.components: 1) core/paths.py: BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; resolve(p) returns absolute p unchanged, else BACKEND_DIR / p. Settings: env_file=BACKEND_DIR/'.env'; validators resolve research_cache_dir, a new state_dir ('.state') and the key dir (T30). Env overrides stay possible. 2) maintenance/runner.py: Step(name, fn); run(steps, trigger) takes the lock, runs each step in its own try/except with a timeout, writes the ledger, releases. Steps: research_cache_purge (T08's purge), retention (sessions idle > 90 days and not saved per D4; anonymous plans with them; consent tombstones older than 1 year; logs older than 30 days), session_upgrade_all (T34), cohort_projection_rebuild (T34 / 5.5.5.2), warming (2.2.6) when it lands. 3) maintenance/lock.py: Redis SET maint:lock <run_id> NX EX 3h; else O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock file in state_dir with pid and start time, stale after 3h. 4) maintenance/ledger.py: state_dir/maintenance.json {step: {last_start, last_success, last_error, consecutive_failures}} written atomically (tmp + os.replace); a table later. Alert = consecutive_failures >= 2, shown by 5.4.3 via GET /internal/maintenance/status. 5) Trigger: POST /internal/maintenance/run (localhost check + MAINTENANCE_TOKEN); scripts/nightly.py posts to it or, on connection refused, runs the runner standalone. App lifespan: if a daily step's last_success is older than 26h, schedule one background catch-up (lock prevents duplicates). Runbook: Windows Task Scheduler entry with 'run as soon as possible after a missed start', and a cron line. 6) services/erasure.py: ERASURE_MAP of every personal table and key path (users.user_id; founders via users.founder_id with startups/profile_completeness/documents cascading; agent_sessions.user_id; plans.user_id; consents -> tombstone) plus non-DB targets (delete_session per id via get_store(), board.forget, result store). erase_user(user_id) refuses '', 'anon' and ids not in users; collects session ids, deletes rows in one transaction, then clears Redis/memory, then writes erasure_log {subject_ref, at, counts}. NOT_PERSONAL lists reference and derived tables. 7) Consent tombstones: on erasure each consent becomes {subject_ref = HMAC(blind_index_key, user_id), purpose, given_at, withdrawn_at, erased_at} with no personal content; deleted 1 year after erased_at. Recorded in SYSTEM-DESIGN 5.4 and decision 0011, flagged for the 3.2.6 legal review.

Erasure selects by owner and refuses until T17 links sessions to real users. Metadata test: set(Base.metadata.tables) == mapped tables | NOT_PERSONAL, so a new table without a decision fails CI.
design.interfaces: T17: real owner ids on sessions (claim) are the precondition for erase_user. T19: consent record shape tombstoned here. T30: hard delete + cascades; blind_index_key reused for subject_ref; key dir via core/paths. T12: board.forget and result-store lifecycle. T08: cache purge semantics (this theme fixes only the path). T34: upgrade-all and projection rebuild as steps; undecodable sessions still deletable by row metadata. T31: plans in the map and retention.

designs.understanding: AgentSession.to_dict/from_dict read and write a fixed key list with no format number. from_dict raises on invalid shapes (ElicitationSession.model_validate, d['updated_at']) and every store calls it unguarded, so one bad document turns a resume into a 500 and fails the whole /programme aggregate (up to 500 sessions loaded in one comprehension). Unknown keys vanish on load-then-save, so rollbacks or mixed deploys strip newer fields such as 'saved'. Removed enum values survive as bare strings under contextlib.suppress(ValueError) and still feed idea_version. SqlStore never upgrades on disk and the row has no format column, so the 5.5.5 split would meet every historical format; and nothing says how split tables stay in step with the JSON truth. Root cause: no codec owns the session document's format (version, decode policy, upgrade chain, guard, projection contract). All five flags hold.

design.components: 1) agents/session_codec.py: FORMAT = 2 (format 1 = today's unversioned docs); UPGRADES = {1: _v1_to_v2}; decode(raw) -> AgentSession; encode(s) -> dict with 'format'. Errors SessionUnreadable(session_id, reason), FormatTooNew(found, known). from_dict/to_dict become private helpers used only by the codec. 2) Stores call decode/encode. get() catches SessionUnreadable, logs agent_store.unreadable and the router maps it to 410 'This conversation cannot be resumed'; FormatTooNew -> 503 'saved by a newer version'. The session remembers loaded_format; save refuses when loaded_format > FORMAT. CachedStore treats an unreadable Redis copy as a miss and drops it. 3) store.get_many(ids) -> (sessions, unreadable_count); /programme returns sessions_unreadable. 4) Vocabulary step: maps slot enum values through T01's old->new mapping; unmapped values cleared with confidence 0 (asked again), never kept as bare strings; if idea_version changes, ResultStore.rekey(session_id, old, new) keeps finished scan/council results. 5) Migration: agent_sessions.format SMALLINT (add nullable, backfill 1, NOT NULL default) and decode_error TEXT NULL. SqlStore writes format on save. 6) scripts/upgrade_sessions.py (also a T32 maintenance step): batches WHERE format < FORMAT; decode -> encode -> versioned UPDATE with the same optimistic guard (skip on conflict); undecodable rows counted and marked in decode_error; idempotent; prints remaining count. 5.5.5.1 precondition: count(format < FORMAT) == 0. 7) Projection (5.5.5.2): analytics tables rebuilt nightly by T32's runner from decoded JSON; nested payloads validated by Pydantic contracts (RoadmapContract from T31, CouncilContract from T35, NoveltyContract); invalid payloads counted, not projected; decision 0012 states JSON is the truth.
design.data_model: Document gains 'format'. agent_sessions gains format SMALLINT NOT NULL and decode_error TEXT NULL. ResultStore gains rekey().
design.algorithm: fmt = raw.get('format', 1); fmt > FORMAT -> FormatTooNew; while fmt < FORMAT: raw = UPGRADES[fmt](deepcopy(raw)); fmt += 1; build AgentSession, mapping KeyError/ValueError/ValidationError to SessionUnreadable. Upgrade functions are pure dict->dict with no ORM imports (enforced by a test).
design.interfaces: T01: canonical vocabulary and old->new mapping. T07: decode policy and get_many join the store contract. T06: idea_version definition decides whether re-keying is needed. T32: upgrade-all and projection rebuild run as maintenance steps. T31/T35: payload contracts. T12: ResultStore.rekey beside its lifecycle work.
design.rollout: 1) Codec with FORMAT=2, decode policy and guard; 2) format column, SqlStore writes it; 3) upgrade-all run once and registered as nightly step; 4) vocabulary step (FORMAT 3) when T01's mapping lands; 5) projection with contracts when 5.5.5 starts.
design.offline: Codec and upgrades run on MemoryStore; the column and script apply only where PostgreSQL exists.

designs.understanding: Claim has only text and evidence, so synthesise() takes the seat that scored a criterion highest or lowest and quotes seat.claims[0] whatever it was about; rules.customer can yield the neutral 'the closest Vanigam domain names its usual buyers' as 'the weakest point'. weights_for adds technical +5 whenever none of seven substrings appears in founder_skills, including when the slot was never asked (it is an enriching slot rarely reached), and misses 'python developer'. convene() makes one ask_seat call per seat (seven) with the full pack in each prompt (pack.lines() without kinds), and seat failures are never recorded on the provider breaker, so a quota-exhausted Gemini costs 8 s every panel. Root cause: the seat output contract lacks what synthesis and weighting need (criterion and direction of a claim; known vs unknown founder skills), and model use is designed per seat although seats share one input. All three flags hold.

flags_disputed.note: A criterion field alone does not fix the probe: the domain-buyers claim is about 'need' but neutral, so it would still be quoted as the weakness. Claims also need a direction (for/against/neutral); synthesis quotes only 'against' claims as weaknesses and 'for' claims as strengths.

design.components: 1) seats.py: Claim{text, evidence, criterion: Literal[CRITERIA] | None, direction: Literal['for','against','neutral']}; validate() drops model claims with a criterion outside CRITERIA; stored opinions without the fields load as neutral and are never quoted for a criterion. 2) rules.py: every rule claim states criterion and direction (local startups exist: need/for; domain names its buyers: need/neutral; no TN startup found: need/against, worded per T13). 3) synthesis.py: strength = highest-confidence 'for' claim with that criterion from any seat (prefer the scoring seat); weakness = an 'against' claim; none -> sentence without the colon clause. 4) vote.py: skills_state(slots) -> technical | non_technical | unknown; unknown when founder_skills was never answered or skipped; technical on a word-boundary match against a reviewed list (software, engineer, electronic, hardware, coding, programming, developer, python, java, embedded, firmware, CAD, electrician, data, web); bump only for non_technical with reason 'founder named no technical skill'. 5) model.py: ask_panel(client, seats, pack, idea, slots, provider): one system prompt (instructions + pack.lines()) and one user message listing each seat's name, brief, question and focus kinds; reply {"opinions": {seat_id: {...}}}; max_tokens about 2500. 6) __init__.py convene: one task with about a 12 s cap; per-seat validate; missing seats -> rules; provider.breaker.fail(reason) on 429/timeout/error and succeed() on success; partial re-runs send only requested seats. 7) Docs: model.py docstring and decision 0009 note ('one call per panel').
